territorial_scope.description: Applies to public sector agencies and private entities deploying AI systems affecting individuals within Oklahoma.

evidence.quote: This act is applicable to all public sector agencies and private entities deploying artificial intelligence (AI) systems affecting individuals within this state.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Oklahoma HB 1916 (introduced) would require public and private deployers of AI systems affecting Oklahomans to classify systems by risk, prohibit unacceptable-risk systems, assess and audit high-risk systems, and create an AI Council, sandbox and workforce grant program, effective November 1, 2025.
summary.long: Oklahoma HB 1916, as introduced, would enact the Responsible Deployment of AI Systems Act (Title 25, Sections 501-511), effective November 1, 2025. It covers public agencies and private entities deploying AI systems affecting individuals in Oklahoma. Deployers must classify systems into four risk categories before deployment, assess them for bias and risks to safety and civil liberties, and notify individuals when high-risk systems influence decisions. High-risk systems require qualified human overseers, ongoing performance evaluations and annual independent audits; deployers must keep governance groups, system inventories and feedback channels. Unacceptable-risk systems are prohibited. A nine-member AI Council, appointed by the Governor and legislative leaders, would run an AI Regulatory Sandbox and a workforce grant program for small businesses and educational institutions. The Council may impose financial penalties, suspend or prohibit noncompliant systems, or require external oversight, and deployers must publicly disclose noncompliance incidents.

notes: Bill as introduced; no legislative history in the text. No penalty amounts are stated; Section 7 lists sanction categories only. Inconsistencies: Section 2(3)(c) refers to 'providers', a term not defined (Section 2 defines 'Deployer'). Section 4(D) says outputs must be validated 'before they are enacted', likely a drafting error. Section 2(3)(a) says prohibited categories 'may include' listed items, so the list is open-ended. Section 4(C) and 5(C) both impose ongoing or annual reviews of high-risk systems, which overlap. Effective date November 1, 2025 (Section 12). Section 6(B) sets a recurring January 1 report date.

thresholds.note: The text contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Numbers present are section numbers, the nine-member AI Council composition in Section 8(C) (a structural rule, not a cutoff), the effective date in Section 12, and the January 1 report date in Section 6(B), which are events. Financial penalties in Section 7(A)(1) are not quantified in this text.
